content: # Git Commit Evidence
Use this module for `tarav-hugentics --commit [PATH...]` and for Git commits
owned by modifying Hugentics workflows. Read-only routes never commit.
Multi-repository work commits each repository independently.
## Routes
The standalone `--commit` invocation authorizes one completion commit in each
selected repository. It creates no artificial start checkpoint. Explicit paths
select their owning repositories and exact worktree scope. Without paths, commit
all current changes in repositories already established by the active task; when
there is no such task scope, use the current Git repository. Do not recursively
discover or absorb unrelated repositories.
A modifying Hugentics workflow instead brackets every repository it mutates with
a scoped start checkpoint and scoped completion commit. Its existing work scope
controls both commits; the initial invocation supplies commit authorization.
## Scope
The agent declares the exact repository-relative paths it is committing.
Do not absorb edits outside the selected scope. At a workflow-owned start, include
only pre-existing changes inside the declared work scope; use an empty
checkpoint when that scope is clean. At completion, include only files the
workflow actually changed. Broader commits require a separate User request.
## Manifest and message
Write a temporary JSON manifest with this shape:
```json
"type": "Tarav.Git.CommitEvidence.Manifest",
"repository": "/absolute/repository",
"files": ["relative/path.py"],

"message": "Subject

- relative/path.py: bounded change
<!-- tarav.context <alias>:<turn-prefix> -->",
"allow_empty": false
Declare sessions in the message with the ordinary `tarav.sessions` block.
Each human-readable `- ` change group ends with one or more provisional
`tarav.context` markers, or with exactly one honest gap marker:
```text
<!-- tarav.evidence agent-initiated -->
<!-- tarav.evidence unknown-session -->
Use `agent-initiated` when the committing agent decided the change without a
supporting User Turn. Use `unknown-session` for pre-existing work whose
discussion cannot be identified. Evidence is best effort; do not fabricate
coverage. Tarav creates Breadcrumb IDs and the recoverable evidence envelope.
Do not author either one manually in a new manifest.
## Commit and recovery
Run:
```bash
tarav git commit --manifest <manifest.json> --json
Tarav validates and registers Breadcrumb evidence, commits only the declared
paths, then records the exact commit-message locations. It preserves staged
changes outside the selection. If Git fails, registered Breadcrumbs may remain
without that location. If the commit exists but observation fails, retain its
hash and recover without another commit:
```bash
tarav breadcrumbs register-commit --repo <repository> --commit <hash> --json
tarav breadcrumbs audit chatlas-context --repo <repository> --commit <hash> --json
If the command fails before committing because evidence cannot be
registered, typically because a sandbox prevents writing to the Tarav data
folder, keep the manifest with its session block and provisional markers
for a later attempt from an environment that can write, and report the
commit as pending, not as done. Do not substitute a plain Git commit whose
message carries provisional markers: `register-commit` recovers only
messages that already hold registered Breadcrumb labels. The read-only
trace left in the changed surfaces remains valid either way.
Write the marker name only in marker lines. A manifest message that
mentions `tarav.context` in ordinary prose is rejected as a malformed
marker.
Inspect the scoped diff and run the relevant checks before every completion
commit. Report each completion hash, Breadcrumb audit result, and honest evidence
gap. Report a start hash only when a composing workflow created one.
